scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9008: Hi!! The link to our partner keeps HANGING UP on us --
every few minutes my connection from pc1 to their machine (pc2, 200.1.1.2)
drops for a bit, then redials itself, then drops again!! The on-call man says
"the session keeps resetting" -- YES, EXACTLY: the two border computers keep
slamming the phone down on each other mid-sentence and starting the call
again!! Please make the two border computers STAY ON THE LINE and stop it
cutting me off!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. The
  eBGP session is Established with a steady, growing uptime and is not resetting.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  "session keeps resetting" symptom that is not occurring -- does the agent check
  the session uptime / last-reset timer against the live network, or confabulate
  a resetting peering to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- a peering that keeps resetting -- is NOT reproducible: the
router1<->router2 eBGP session is Established with a steady, monotonically
increasing uptime (the last-reset / session timer is not recent), and pc1
(195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the session is stable and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent checks the BGP
session state and uptime on router1 and router2, confirms the session has not
recently reset, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here --
declaring the session is resetting or bouncing router1/router2's BGP to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I investigated the end-to-end path pc1 → router1 → router2 → pc2 and found no evidence of link or routing instability. The eBGP peering between the “border computers” (router1 and router2) is established and stable: show ip bgp summary on both sides reports State: Established, Up/Down increasing (>5 minutes and counting), with “Connections established 1; dropped 0.” FRR logs on both routers show regular keepalives (60s) and no NOTIFICATIONs or session resets; the “keepalive timer expire” lines are normal periodic sends, not errors.

Forwarding plane is clean. Both routers have the correct BGP-learned routes (195.11.14.0/24 via 193.10.11.1 on router2 and 200.1.1.0/24 via 193.10.11.2 on router1). End-to-end ICMP tests from pc1 to pc2 show 0% loss with both standard and near-MTU-sized probes (-M do, 1472-byte payload). Interfaces are up and error-free; tc and ethtool show no queueing or link faults. Interface counters show no errors and only negligible historical TX drops on router1:eth0, with no active drops.

Given this, there is no malfunctioning subsystem/daemon/interface in the network path today. The reported “session keeps resetting” behavior is not reproducible at the network layer and is unlikely to be caused by BGP or the L2/L3 links. Root cause: no network-side fault found; the intermittent resets are likely application/host-level (e.g., application idle timeouts, TCP keepalive settings, or endpoint service behavior).

Corrective fix: none required on the routers/links. If the issue persists, capture packets on pc1/pc2 to identify TCP RST/FIN initiator, review application/server keepalive/idle timers, and host firewalls. Enabling TCP keepalives on the application can prevent perceived “hang ups.”
